name: SC-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+13 partisan lean as a majority-Black Democratic seat
Clyburn's three-decade incumbency and $1.6 million cash advantage
Challenger John Peterson shows no reported fundraising or campaign infrastructure
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds around 96 percent
model.rationale: The seat's thirteen-point Democratic lean, Clyburn's standing as one of the House's longest-serving members, and his overwhelming financial edge leave the underfunded Republican challenger without a visible path, and market pricing near 96 percent aligns with those fundamentals.
model.watch: Only an unexpected late development, such as redistricting changes or a major scandal, would move this race toward competitive territory.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District is a majority-Black seat drawn to favor Democrats, with a partisan lean of roughly thirteen points. Jim Clyburn, first elected in 1992 and among the most senior figures in the House, has routinely won reelection by wide margins and enters the cycle with more than $1.6 million on hand. His Republican opponent, John Peterson, reports no fundraising and has little visible campaign presence.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and incumbency. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 96 percent, consistent with a safe seat. The main uncertainty is turnout variation in a low-profile contest rather than a genuine competitive threat, and the expected margin remains in the low twenties.
